title: Ishaan Khatter Joins the Biarritz Film Festival Jury. He'll Sit Alongside Kristen Stewart as the Only Indian Panelist.
excerpt: The actor joins an international jury for the Nouvelles Vagues edition in France, continuing a rise that's taken him from Bollywood to Gold House to European festival circuits.
body:
Ishaan Khatter will sit alongside Kristen Stewart at one of Europe's most closely watched emerging cinema festivals this June — and he'll be the only Indian on the jury.

The actor has been invited to join the jury panel at the Biarritz Film Festival – Nouvelles Vagues 2026, the French festival's fourth edition, scheduled from June 23 to 28 in the seaside city of Biarritz in southern France. The jury will be chaired by Kristen Stewart, with a lineup that includes Canadian actress Whitney Peak, French actor-director Raphaël Quenard, filmmaker Nathan Ambrosioni, Suzy Bemba, Italian director Carolina Cavalli, and British actress Esmé Creed-Miles.

## Why This Matters

The Biarritz Film Festival – Nouvelles Vagues focuses specifically on cinema centered around younger generations and emerging voices. It's not Cannes in scale, but it has rapidly become a significant platform for contemporary storytelling and new creative talent from around the world. Having an Indian actor on the jury panel — not as a guest, not as a presenter, but as someone whose vote shapes which films get recognized — is a meaningful step.

Ishaan's inclusion follows a trajectory that's been building for a while. His performance in Mira Nair's *A Suitable Boy* introduced him to international audiences. *The Royals* expanded that footprint. His recent project *Homebound* received appreciation in festival and critical circles. And earlier this year, he was featured on the Gold House Gold 100 list — the only Indian male actor on the annual ranking of influential Asian and Pacific figures across industries.

## The Broader Pattern

Ishaan's festival appointment is part of a broader shift in how Indian actors are engaging with global cinema institutions. It's no longer just about attending premieres or walking red carpets. Deepika Padukone served on the Cannes jury in 2022. Indian films have been increasingly present at Venice, Toronto, and Berlin. But jury appointments at European festivals dedicated to emerging cinema represent a different kind of recognition — one that's less about star power and more about creative credibility.

## What's Next for Ishaan

On the work front, Ishaan will next be seen in *Jugaadu*, a comic caper that doubles as his first production venture. He shared the first look on Instagram earlier this month.

For the Indian diaspora watching from abroad, Ishaan Khatter's growing international presence offers a version of Bollywood's next chapter that isn't defined by box office numbers alone. It's defined by who gets to decide which stories matter — and now, an Indian voice is at that table in Biarritz.
author: Diaspora Desk
